transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because... well, I keep thinking it would be better if I just didn't wake up. Honestly, sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew.
Have you thought about how you would carry out your death if you were to act on these feelings?

I don't really have a specific plan. Like I just said, it's mostly just... hoping I go to sleep and don't wake up. I haven't figured out a way to do it myself. I just have this constant feeling that I deserve it, that dying is the only fair punishment for everything I've put my family and my crew through.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up?

It's been with me for about a year and two months now. It started... well, a few months after my husband's injury. That's when this depression really set in, and I just haven't been able to shake it since.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy before your husband's injury?

No, not really. I used to do a lot of things... I'd paint, cook these big meals, go for a run before my flooring jobs, and I'd always show up for theater rehearsals. But now... honestly, those things just feel like chores from somebody else's life. I don't get anything out of them anymore, and I just don't care if I miss them.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?
No, not really. I mean, I don't feel nervous or anything like that. It's more just... this heavy feeling all the time. I'm just so tired and down, but I wouldn't say I feel anxious.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight over the past year?

Yeah, I have. My work pants have gotten really loose on me lately, and I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything. Most days I just... I forget to eat until it's really late. Or if I do try to eat, I'll take a few bites and just feel sick to my stomach.
Do you feel like you've been moving more slowly than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm tired all the time, but I wouldn't say I'm physically moving in slow motion or anything like that. I just... I just don't have the energy to do much, but when I do move, it feels normal, I guess.
Have you had periods of depression like this before your husband's injury?

No, I haven't. Before he got hurt, things were... well, they were pretty normal. I mean, everyone has bad days sometimes, but I never felt anything like this. This whole heavy, empty feeling really just started after his accident. I definitely never felt this way before that.
Have you had any periods where your depression symptoms were significantly worse than they are now?

No, I wouldn't say they've been worse. It's just been a constant... well, a constant low since the accident. It hasn't really spiked or gotten worse at any specific point, it's just always there. The same heavy feeling every day.
Would you describe your current depression as mild, moderate, or severe?

I'd say it's severe. It really takes a toll on me... just getting through the day is incredibly hard. I don't think it could be just mild or moderate, not with how empty and exhausted I feel all the time.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to find pleasurable, such as painting, cooking, or theater rehearsals, consistently over the past two weeks?

Yes, I have. I used to do all of that. I used to paint, and I'd cook big meals... I'd even go for a run before heading out to my flooring jobs, and I always showed up for theater rehearsals. But now... I don't know, those things just feel like chores from somebody else's life. I really just don't care if I miss them anymore.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?

Yes, I have. Um... I actually hear a man's voice sometimes. It usually happens when I'm at job sites, or even just in my kitchen. He speaks from right behind me and says things like... well, he tells me I missed it, or that everyone knows. It sounds clear as day, exactly as if someone is standing right there. But whenever I turn around to look, nobody is there.
Have you ever seen things that other people couldn't see, like shadows or figures, in addition to hearing the voice?

No, I haven't seen anything like that. Um, no shadows or figures. Like I just mentioned, it's really just the voice. I just hear that man's voice right behind me at the job sites or in the kitchen saying things like "you missed it" or "everyone knows." It sounds incredibly clear, like he's standing right there, but when I actually turn around to look, nobody's there. I don't see anyone or anything.
Have you ever believed things that weren't true, like thinking people are against you or plotting something, when there's no evidence for it?

Yes. Um, even when I'm not feeling completely down or stuck in bed crying, I get this... this absolute certainty that people are against me. I get certain that the homeowners and the suppliers are tracking me. I believe they're using the floor patterns I lay down, the text messages, and even the permit calls to track whether I'm ruining the jobs on purpose. And, honestly, no one can talk me out of it when I get like that. It just feels so real.
Are the voices you hear and the beliefs that people are against you happening at the same time as your depressive feelings?

Yes, they do happen at the same time. Um, during those months when I was... when I was barely eating, just wishing I wouldn't wake up in the morning, and blaming myself for absolutely everything... I was also hearing that man's voice. And I was also completely convinced that the job calls and the floor patterns were meant to expose me. So, yes, it all happens together.
Do you ever hear the voice or have those beliefs that people are against you when you're not feeling depressed?

Yes. There was actually a stretch of several weeks where I was doing a bit better. I was getting up, eating a little better, and I wasn't crying all day. But... I still heard the voice at work. And I stayed completely convinced that the clients and suppliers were tracking me. So, yes, those things still happen even when I'm not feeling depressed.
Do the voice and beliefs that people are against you only happen when you're feeling depressed?

No, it's not just when I'm depressed. Like I was just saying, um, there was a stretch of several weeks where my mood was actually okay. I was getting out of bed, I was eating, I wasn't crying all the time. But even during those weeks, I still heard that voice while I was installing flooring. And I was still absolutely certain that the clients and the suppliers were tracking me. So, the voice and the beliefs don't go away just because the depression lifts for a bit.
Are the voice and beliefs that people are against you ever present when you're not feeling depressed or having any depressive symptoms?

Yes, like I mentioned, they definitely are. I had a few weeks where my mood had actually improved—I was getting up, eating better, and the crying stopped. But even then, I was still hearing the voice while I was working on the floors, and I still believed the clients and suppliers were keeping tabs on me. So those things don't just disappear when the depression gets better.
Are the voice and beliefs that people are against you only present when you're feeling depressed?

No, it's not just when I'm depressed. I know I've said this a few times now, but there was a period of a few weeks where I felt better. I was getting out of bed, my appetite was a little better, and I wasn't crying. But I was still hearing the voice while I was installing flooring. And I was still completely sure that the clients and suppliers were tracking my movements. So, no, they don't only happen when I'm depressed.
Are the voice and beliefs that people are against you ever present when you're feeling completely normal and not having any depressive symptoms?

Yes... I feel like we're going in circles a bit here, but yes. Like I keep saying, there was that stretch of several weeks where I felt pretty normal. I was getting up, eating a little better, and not crying all day. But even then, I still heard the voice at work, and I stayed convinced that the clients and suppliers were tracking me. So even when I'm not feeling depressed at all, those things are still happening.
